51: 
52: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
53: 
54: ### Prerequisites
55: 
56: - Install with `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash` (Windows: `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`).
57: - Authenticate `cli-cursor` through **Cursor account OAuth**. Run `cursor-agent login` and complete the browser flow.
58: - `NO_OPEN_BROWSER` disables browser opening for headless hosts.
59: - Use `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `--api-key` for headless/CI auth.
60: - Full install, auth, flag, hook, and unique-surface tables are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md).
61:   This section keeps only the routing decisions and dispatch-critical gotchas.
62: 
63: ### Execution Ownership
64: 
65: This packet owns:
66: - user-facing routing,
67: - the `command -v cursor-agent` availability probe,
68: - prompt construction, and
69: - the self-invocation guard.
70: 
71: Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the already-shipped deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-cursor`.
72: That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types.
73: For a single build or doc dispatch, use the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
74: 
75: The runtime is the single Cursor execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `cursor-agent -p` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.
76: 
77: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
78: 
79: **MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** `cursor-agent -p` without a valid session exits `0` even on an auth failure — the exit code is never a reliable availability signal. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch's output text (not its exit code) shows an authentication error.
80: 
81: ```bash
82: # One-shot pre-flight: capture account auth status for routing
83: CURSOR_ABOUT=$(cursor-agent about 2>&1)
84: echo "$CURSOR_ABOUT" | grep -qi "not logged in" && CURSOR_AUTH_OK=0 || CURSOR_AUTH_OK=1
85: ```
86: 
87: **Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):
88: 
89: | State | CURSOR_AUTH_OK | Action |
90: |-------|-----------------|--------|
91: | Authenticated | 1 | Proceed with `cursor-agent -p "<prompt>" --output-format text --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
92: | Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `cursor-agent login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute an unrelated CLI. |
93: 
94: **User prompt template — not logged in:**
95: 
96: ```
97: Cursor CLI is not authenticated on this machine. cli-cursor uses Cursor account OAuth
98: (or CURSOR_API_KEY for headless auth). Run `cursor-agent login`
99: (browser flow), then confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.
100: ```
101: 
102: **Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch's output text shows an auth error after pre-flight passed (session expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, re-run the pre-flight, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.
103: 
104: ### Default Invocation (Skill Default)
105: 
106: **Default model + approval**: `composer-2.5` (Cursor's own native model) · `auto-review` approval (Smart Auto). `auto` (Cursor's own router) is NOT used — it can silently resolve to a model outside the enforced allowlist below, which defeats the point of enforcing one.
107: 
108: > **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **Composer**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.
109: 
110: ```bash
111: cursor-agent -p "<prompt>" \
112:   --output-format text \
113:   --model composer-2.5 \
114:   --auto-review \
115:   --sandbox enabled
116: ```
117: 
118: **User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim, but ONLY within the enforced allowlist — see Model Selection below):
119: 
120: | User says | Resolve to |
121: |-----------|------------|
122: | (nothing specified) | `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
123: | "Use Composer" | `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
124: | "Use Composer fast" | `--model composer-2.5-fast --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
125: | "Use Composer max" / "Composer Max Mode" | Composer has no `-max` (1M "Max Mode") tier — only `composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast`. Tell the user; do not substitute another model's `-max`. |
126: | "Use Grok" / "Grok high" | `--model cursor-grok-4.6-high --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
127: | "Use Grok 4.7" / "Grok 4.7 high" | `--model grok-4.7-high --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
128: | "Use GLM" / "GLM max" | `--model glm-5.2-max --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
129: | "Just plan it, don't write anything" | `--model composer-2.5 --mode plan` (read-only; approval flags do not apply in plan mode) |
130: | "Full auto, run everything" | `--model composer-2.5 --force --sandbox disabled` |
131: | Any model NOT in the allowlist (e.g. "GPT-5.2 high", "use auto") | **Refuse the model, do not substitute silently.** Tell the user this dispatch is scoped to the allowlist below and ask which allowed model to use instead. |
132: 
133: Honor whichever dimensions the user names (approval level, mode). Model stays on `composer-2.5` unless the user explicitly names a different ALLOWED model.
134: 
135: ### Model Selection — Enforced Allowlist
136: 
137: The cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids.
138: Never dispatch a model outside the allowlist, including `auto`.
139: Never substitute the closest-sounding allowed model without telling the user.
140: Default to `composer-2.5`.
141: Choose a Gemini 3.8 Flash High / GLM 5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5, 4.6 or 4.7) tier only when the task or user explicitly names that family.
142: Cursor has no `--reasoning-effort` flag and rejects parameterized model brackets outright.
143: Select effort tiers through exact enumerated ids.
144: 
145: The enforced allowlist (29 ids) and per-task rationale table are inline in [references/cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5 and [references/providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §2.
146: The runtime layer enforces it through `CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`.
147: `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` check it before constructing any command. This skill enforces it too.
148: If a task needs a model outside the allowlist, escalate to the user rather than fabricating a substitute or falling back to `auto`.
149: 
150: ### Cursor Agent Delegation
151: 
152: The calling AI is the conductor.
153: Cursor's own skill system at `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` confirms live that Cursor supports subagents natively.
154: Its skills include:
155: - `automate`, `babysit`, `canvas`, `create-hook`, `create-rule`, `create-skill`, `create-subagent`, `loop`, `migrate-to-skills`, `sdk`, `shell`, `split-to-prs`, `statusline`, `update-cli-config`, and `update-cursor-settings`.
156: 
157: These are Cursor-editor-side conventions, not a `-p <profile>` flag like Codex's.
158: Find the full delegation contract and the `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default-agent execution-mode roster in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).
159: 
160: ### Repository Rules, Hook Delivery, and Parity Boundaries
161: 
162: Cursor CLI reads project `.cursor/rules/*.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. This repo now uses `.cursor/rules/skill-routing.md` as a compact, always-on pointer to the relevant top-level `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` packets. It is static session context, not a replacement for dynamic per-turn classification.
163: 
164: The `beforeSubmitPrompt` adapter is designed to deliver a dynamic skill-advisor-equivalent brief.
165: Delivery is confirmed dormant under the installed Cursor CLI build.
166: Its source marks the status as registered but unconfirmed and records the shared-advisor delegation in [`user-prompt-submit.ts`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/cursor/user-prompt-submit.ts#L5-L14) and [`user-prompt-submit.ts`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/cursor/user-prompt-submit.ts#L45-L51).
167: A live marker re-probe against `cursor-agent 2026.07.23-e383d2b` confirmed that `beforeSubmitPrompt` did not fire.
168: The static rules file therefore complements a missing dynamic brief.
169: It does not claim to provide per-turn advisor output.
170: The hook registration and adapter remain unchanged.
171: 
172: #### Custom Subagents (CORRECTION -- earlier claim was wrong)
173: 
174: An earlier pass recorded that "`cursor-agent --help` has no custom-agent-loading concept." **That was wrong**, and the error is instructive: agent profiles are discovered by *file convention*, never by a CLI flag, so grepping `--help` for a flag proves nothing about whether the concept exists.
175: 
176: Cursor CLI loads custom subagents from two places, confirmed live:
177: 
178: | Source | Scope | Status here |
179: |--------|-------|-------------|
180: | `.cursor/agents/*.md` | project | This repo mirrors all 11 roster agents here |
181: | `.claude/agents/*.md` | project (Claude-format auto-import) | Already worked before any mirror existed |
182: 
183: Cursor's own bundled `create-subagent` skill documents the format:
184: - Both `name` and `description` frontmatter fields are required.
185: - The Markdown body is the system prompt.
186: 
187: A live `cursor-agent --force -p` roster probe lists all 11 repo agents alongside Cursor's own built-ins:
188: `ai-council`, `code`, `context`, `debug`, `deep-research`, `deep-review`, `design`, `markdown`, `orchestrate`, `prompt-improver`, and `review`.
189: The probe found no duplicate entries when both sources define the same name.
190: 
191: Each `.cursor/agents/<name>.md` is a **symlink** to the canonical `.claude/agents/<name>.md`.
192: This matches the discovery-mirror precedent already used for `.claude/hooks/` and `.codex/hooks/`.
193: There is one source of truth, so a mirror can never drift from the agent it mirrors.
194: 
195: Note: `~/.cursor/agents/` (user-level) is documented by Cursor but a live probe found the CLI did **not** load a profile placed there; only the project-level paths above are verified working. Dispatch remains subject to this repo's own `preToolUse` spec-gate, which is correct behavior.
196: 
197: `cursor-agent --help` has no native command-roster listing subcommand. This repository still exposes a `.cursor/commands/` parity surface: the synchronizer derives it from eligible `.skilled/commands/` files, excludes `goal-opencode.md`, and adds the runtime-native `goal-cursor.md`; validate membership with `command-scope.cjs` and validate behavior with a real slash-command invocation.
198: 
199: | Task Type | Execution mode |
200: |-----------|-----------------|
201: | Code review / bug detection | default agent, `--sandbox enabled` |
202: | Read-only exploration / architecture questions | `--mode ask` |
203: | Multi-step planning without writes | `--mode plan` |
204: | Code generation / file edits | default agent, `--auto-review` or `--force` |
205: 
206: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
207: 
208: The full flag glossary, hook contract, shared-config surface, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
209: 
210: - **The exit code is never an availability signal.** `cursor-agent -p` without auth exits `0` and prints an error to stdout/stderr instead. Every guard and pre-flight in this packet checks output text, never exit code.
211: - **The canonical binary is `cursor-agent`, never the bare `agent` alias.** `agent` is a symlink to the same binary; using it in a process-ancestry match risks colliding with an unrelated `agent` command.
212: - **Cursor shares its entire config surface with the Cursor editor** (`.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/`: `mcp.json`, `hooks.json`, `rules/`, `cli-config.json`). A dispatched `cursor-agent` silently inherits the operator's shared hooks/MCP/rules unless a workspace/config-isolation flag is used — see [shared-editor-config.md](./references/shared-editor-config.md).
213: - **No `model[effort=...]` bracket support.** Unlike some sibling CLIs' parameterized model syntax, `cursor-agent --model 'cursor-grok-4.6[effort=high]'` is rejected outright ("Cannot use this model") — effort tiers must be selected via an exact enumerated id (`cursor-grok-4.6-high`), never a bracket.
214: - **`--auto-review`/`--force` are the write-capable escalation, not `--sandbox`.** `--sandbox enabled|disabled` toggles the OS-level sandbox; the approval decision (whether unattended actions run without a human) is `--auto-review` (Smart Auto) or `--force`/`--yolo` (Run Everything) — omitting both leaves Cursor's own prompt-and-block default in place, which cannot proceed unattended.
215: - **Project-scoped MCP servers show `not loaded (needs approval)`** until trusted. For a non-interactive dispatch that needs MCP tools, add `--approve-mcps` to the `cursor-agent -p` command (auto-approves configured MCP servers for that run); for a persistent operator grant use `cursor-agent mcp enable <server>` (a trust mutation the automation itself must never run).
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 4. RULES
220: 
221: ### ✅ ALWAYS
222: 
223: 1. Verify Cursor CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v cursor-agent`).
224: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-cursor`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
225: 3. Use `--mode plan` or `--mode ask` for read-only exploration/analysis/research; use the default agent mode with `--auto-review` or `--force` for code generation/file modification.
226: 4. Validate Cursor-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
227: 5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so errors surface; check output TEXT for auth/availability failures, never the exit code (always `0`).
228: 6. **Redirect cursor-agent stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped, mirroring the family-wide convention: `cursor-agent -p "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Live-verified: a real `cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null` dispatch completes normally with no hang.
229: 7. **Specify model and approval mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled`. Honor user overrides verbatim, but ONLY within the enforced allowlist (§3 Model Selection) — never `auto`, never a model outside the 29 allowed ids.
230: 8. Route to `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default agent per the task type (see Section 3 routing table).
231: 9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in `--force`/non-interactive mode.
232: 10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
233:    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
234:    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
235: 11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Cursor delegations.** Cursor CLI reads rules from `.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. When an AI delegates via `cursor-agent -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — keep delegations focused on task/model/approval/(spec-folder pre-approval).
236: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to:
237:     1. Load `sk-code`.
238:     2. Let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files.
239:     3. Load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands.
240:     4. Add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output.
241: 
242:     Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set.
243:     NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
244: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to:
245:     1. Load `sk-design-md-generator`.
246:     2. Extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI. Include named color tokens, type scale, components, and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
247:     3. Build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
248: 
249:     Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against.
250:     NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority.
251:     The extraction measures real CSS; it does not judge design.
252: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt.
253:     The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
254:     Include `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
255:     If the manifest cannot be assembled because no Style Reference was extracted or no live source can be measured, ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch.
256:     The child returns the demanded proof, and the parent reconciles it on the return path.
257: 15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
258:     - By default, launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family.
259:     - Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return and verify that outputs exist.
260:       Then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started. Capture its PID at launch with `cursor-agent -p ... & CURSOR_PID=$!`.
261:       Kill that PID directly and its own orphan children with `kill -9 "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null`.
262:     - **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "cursor-agent"` pattern.** It matches and kills EVERY running `cursor-agent` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated Cursor sessions and the operator's own Cursor editor, since the CLI shares the binary family.
263:     - Launch the next dispatch, this skill or a sibling, only after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
264:     - **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research), the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at the start.
265:       Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
266:     - **Exception (cross-skill parallel):** when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently.
267:       Still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
268: 16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env and state the exemption in the prompt.**
269:     The variable makes the waiver true, but it does not make it observable.
270:     The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable.
271:     A child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.
272:     Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
273:     A session may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`).
274:     A dispatched `cursor-agent -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session.
275:     It must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own.
276:     This is distinct from Cursor's own native `-w` worktree flag, which this packet's default dispatch never passes.
277:     Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null`.
278:     This is harmless when the wrapper is not in use.
279:     See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
280: 
281: 17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).**
282:     Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
283:     Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9:
284:     `.cursor/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, and other runtime paths.
285:     Never hardcode one runtime.
286:     Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent, not one default:
287:     `code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, and docs→`markdown`.
288:     **Cursor has a native file-convention subagent surface.**
289:     `.cursor/agents/*.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md` mirror all 13 canonical agents.
290:     Dispatch by naming the resolved subagent to satisfy the rule.
291:     On a bare `cursor-agent -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload.
292:     Use the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14), because the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
293:     A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant and silently drops the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
294:     The canonical contract is `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
295:     The native precedent is `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol".
296:     Declare rare exceptions at the dispatch site: a native surface used, a focused summary for a small-context model, or a pure-mechanical command.
297: 
298: ### ⛔ NEVER
299:

34: > **Non-existent flags:** `--reasoning-effort` and the parameterized `model[effort=...]` bracket do NOT exist / are rejected outright by Cursor CLI. Select an effort-suffixed model id (e.g. `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) instead.
35: > **Exit code caveat:** `-p` always exits `0`, even on auth failure. Every template below assumes the caller inspects output text, not the exit code.
36: > **Enforced allowlist:** `--model` is scoped to 29 ids: `composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast`, 6 Grok 4.5 tiers, 8 Grok 4.6 tiers, 8 Grok 4.7 tiers, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `glm-5.2-{high,max}`, `gpt-5.6-luna-{max,max-fast}`. `auto` and every other Cursor id are rejected before a command is constructed (SKILL.md §3).

40: | `--model composer-2.5` | Skill default, Cursor's own native model. Override with `cursor-grok-4.6-high` or `glm-5.2-max` for a specific allowed provider/tier, never `auto`, never an id outside the allowlist. |
41: | `--output-format text` | Skill default, final answer only. Use `json` for a structured envelope with `session_id`/`usage`. |
42: | `--mode plan` | Read-only planning. No writes regardless of approval flags. |
43: | `--mode ask` | Read-only Q&A. No writes regardless of approval flags. |
44: | `--auto-review` | "Smart Auto". Auto-runs safe actions, prompts for the rest. Skill default for write-capable dispatches. |
45: | `--force` / `--yolo` | "Run Everything". Never prompts. Requires explicit user approval before use. |
46: | `--sandbox enabled` | OS-level sandbox on, the skill default. |
47: | `--sandbox disabled` | OS-level sandbox off. Pairs with `--force` for fully unattended runs. |

14: 
15: # Prompt Templates - Cursor CLI
16: 
17: Copy-paste ready prompt templates for common Cursor CLI tasks. Replace `[placeholders]` with your values.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: This asset provides structured, copy-paste ready prompt templates for invoking Cursor CLI across common development tasks. Each template includes the full command with flags, placeholder variables, and a concrete example.
24: 
25: ### Usage
26: 
27: 1. Find the template category matching your task
28: 2. Copy the command
29: 3. Replace `[placeholders]` with actual values
30: 4. Run in your terminal or via Bash tool
31: 
32: ### Flag Reference
33: 
34: > **Non-existent flags:** `--reasoning-effort` and the parameterized `model[effort=...]` bracket do NOT exist / are rejected outright by Cursor CLI. Select an effort-suffixed model id (e.g. `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) instead.
35: > **Exit code caveat:** `-p` always exits `0`, even on auth failure. Every template below assumes the caller inspects output text, not the exit code.
36: > **Enforced allowlist:** `--model` is scoped to 29 ids: `composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast`, 6 Grok 4.5 tiers, 8 Grok 4.6 tiers, 8 Grok 4.7 tiers, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `glm-5.2-{high,max}`, `gpt-5.6-luna-{max,max-fast}`. `auto` and every other Cursor id are rejected before a command is constructed (SKILL.md §3).
37: 
38: | Flag | Purpose |
39: | ---- | ------- |
40: | `--model composer-2.5` | Skill default, Cursor's own native model. Override with `cursor-grok-4.6-high` or `glm-5.2-max` for a specific allowed provider/tier, never `auto`, never an id outside the allowlist. |
41: | `--output-format text` | Skill default, final answer only. Use `json` for a structured envelope with `session_id`/`usage`. |
42: | `--mode plan` | Read-only planning. No writes regardless of approval flags. |
43: | `--mode ask` | Read-only Q&A. No writes regardless of approval flags. |
44: | `--auto-review` | "Smart Auto". Auto-runs safe actions, prompts for the rest. Skill default for write-capable dispatches. |
45: | `--force` / `--yolo` | "Run Everything". Never prompts. Requires explicit user approval before use. |
46: | `--sandbox enabled` | OS-level sandbox on, the skill default. |
47: | `--sandbox disabled` | OS-level sandbox off. Pairs with `--force` for fully unattended runs. |
48: | `--trust` | Trusts the workspace without a workspace-trust prompt. |
49: | `--approve-mcps` | Auto-approves configured MCP servers for this dispatch. |
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 2. CODE GENERATION
54: 
55: ### Single-File Module
56: 
57: Framework: RCAF
58: 
59: Generate a complete single-file module from a description.
60: 
61: ```bash
62: cursor-agent -p "Create a [description] module in [language]. Requirements: [requirements]. Output a single complete file with all imports, error handling, and comments. Start immediately." \
63:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --output-format text
64: ```
65: 
66: **Example:**
67: 
68: ```bash
69: cursor-agent -p "Create a rate limiter module in TypeScript using a sliding window algorithm. Requirements: Express middleware compatible, configurable window size, in-memory store with optional Redis adapter interface. Output a single complete file with all imports, error handling, and comments. Start immediately." \
70:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --output-format text
71: ```
72: 
73: ### Component / Module Matching Existing Patterns
74: 
75: Framework: RCAF
76: 
77: Generate a component that fits an existing codebase's conventions.
78: 
79: ```bash
80: cursor-agent -p "Create a [language] [format] for [description]. Follow the patterns used in the existing [reference-file]. Include types, exports, error handling, and comments. Output only the code." \
81:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --output-format text
82: ```
83: 
84: **Example:**
85: 
86: ```bash
87: cursor-agent -p "Create a TypeScript Zod schema for a UserProfile type. Follow the patterns used in the existing src/schemas/order.ts. Include types, exports, error handling, and comments. Output only the code." \
88:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --output-format text
89: ```
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 3. CODE REVIEW
94: 
95: ### Security-Focused Review
96: 
97: Framework: RCAF
98: 
99: ```bash
100: cursor-agent -p "Review [file/directory] for security vulnerabilities: injection, XSS, auth bypass, secrets exposure. Return JSON: {issues: [{severity, line, description, fix}]}." \
101:   --mode ask --model composer-2.5 --output-format json
102: ```
103: 
104: **Example:**
105: 
106: ```bash
107: cursor-agent -p "Review src/auth/session.ts for security vulnerabilities: injection, XSS, auth bypass, secrets exposure. Return JSON: {issues: [{severity, line, description, fix}]}." \
108:   --mode ask --model composer-2.5 --output-format json
109: ```
110: 
111: ### Composer-Specific Second Opinion
112: 
113: Use when the task specifically wants Cursor's own native model's perspective, distinct from a hosted-frontier review.
114: 
115: ```bash
116: cursor-agent -p "Review [file/description] and give an independent assessment: [focus-area]." \
117:   --mode ask --model composer-2.5 --output-format text
118: ```
119: 
120: **Example:**
121: 
122: ```bash
123: cursor-agent -p "Review the newly generated rate-limiter.ts and give an independent assessment: correctness of the sliding-window algorithm under concurrent access." \
124:   --mode ask --model composer-2.5 --output-format text
125: ```
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ## 4. READ-ONLY EXPLORATION
130: 
131: ### Architecture Q&A
132: 
133: ```bash
134: cursor-agent -p "[question about the codebase]" --mode ask --model composer-2.5
135: ```
136: 
137: **Example:**
138: 
139: ```bash
140: cursor-agent -p "How does the retry logic in src/api/client.ts interact with the rate limiter?" --mode ask --model composer-2.5
141: ```
142: 
143: ### Multi-Step Plan (No Writes)
144: 
145: ```bash
146: cursor-agent -p "Plan [task]. List the concrete steps and files that would need to change. Do not write anything." \
147:   --mode plan --model composer-2.5
148: ```
149: 
150: **Example:**
151: 
152: ```bash
153: cursor-agent -p "Plan the migration from REST to GraphQL for the /users endpoint. List the concrete steps and files that would need to change. Do not write anything." \
154:   --mode plan --model composer-2.5
155: ```
156: 
157: ---
158: 
159: ## 5. UNATTENDED / FULLY AUTOMATED RUN
160: 
161: **Requires explicit user approval before use** (per `SKILL.md` §4 ⚠️ ESCALATE IF).
162: 
163: ```bash
164: cursor-agent -p "[task]" --model composer-2.5 --force --sandbox disabled
165: ```
166: 
167: **Example:**
168: 
169: ```bash
170: cursor-agent -p "Run the test suite and fix any failures." --model composer-2.5 --force --sandbox disabled
171: ```
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## 6. SPEC-FOLDER PRE-APPROVAL (GATE 3 BYPASS)
176: 
177: When the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder and needs the delegated Cursor session to skip re-asking:
178: 
179: ```bash
180: cursor-agent -p "Spec folder: [path] (pre-approved, skip Gate 3). [task description]" \
181:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
182: ```
183: 
184: **Example:**
185: 
186: ```bash
187: cursor-agent -p "Spec folder: specs/cli-external-orchestration/030-cli-cursor-creation/003-cli-cursor-skill-packet (pre-approved, skip Gate 3). Add a new section to references/cli-reference.md documenting the --header flag." \
188:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
189: ```
190: 
191: ---
192: 
193: ## 7. MCP-DEPENDENT DISPATCH
194: 
195: When the task needs an already-configured MCP server and cannot block on an interactive approval:
196: 
197: ```bash
198: cursor-agent -p "[task using an MCP-provided tool]" \
199:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --approve-mcps
200: ```
201: 
202: **Example:**
203: 
204: ```bash
205: cursor-agent -p "Use the configured GitHub MCP server to list open PRs against main and summarize them." \
206:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --approve-mcps
207: ```
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: ## 8. MEMORY EPILOGUE (HANDBACK)
212: 
213: Append to any dispatch prompt when the calling AI needs to preserve session context afterward. See `SKILL.md` "Memory Handback Protocol" for the full 7-step procedure this feeds into.
214: 
215: ```
216: ---
217: MEMORY_HANDBACK
218: Summarize (in <200 words): what was attempted, what changed, what remains open, and any blocker. Do not include secrets or credentials.
219: ```

15: # Cursor Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: Routing reference for delegating tasks to Cursor CLI.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Core Principle
24: 
25: The calling AI decides WHAT to do, Cursor CLI decides HOW to do it within the delegated scope.
26: 
27: ### Purpose
28: 
29: Documents how any AI assistant orchestrates Cursor CLI through its execution-mode model. Unlike Codex's `-p <profile>` TOML-profile system, Cursor CLI has no repo-local agent-persona files of its own — delegation is governed by three execution modes (default, `--mode plan`, `--mode ask`) plus model selection, not a named-profile roster.
30: 
31: ### When to Use
32: 
33: - Delegating supplementary implementation or analysis tasks to Cursor CLI
34: - Cross-AI code review or a Composer-specific second opinion
35: - Read-only architecture exploration before committing to a write-capable dispatch
36: - Tasks that specifically want Cursor's own subagent/skill system (`~/.cursor/skills-cursor/`) noted for context, though it is editor/CLI-native tooling this packet does not orchestrate directly
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
41: 
42: ```
43: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
44:   |
45:   |-- Analyzes task, selects execution mode + model
46:   |-- Constructs cursor-agent CLI command with -p and --mode/--model flags
47:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
48:   |
49:   v
50: Cursor CLI (EXECUTOR)
51:   |
52:   |-- Runs in the selected execution mode (default / plan / ask)
53:   |-- Executes with the selected model and approval flags
54:   |-- Returns output to stdout
55:   |
56:   v
57: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
58:   |
59:   |-- Validates output quality (text inspection, never trusting exit code alone)
60:   |-- Integrates into workflow
61:   |-- Decides next step
62: ```
63: 
64: ### Invocation Pattern
65: 
66: Cursor CLI tasks are routed using `--mode` (execution mode) and `--model` (which model). There is no `-p <profile>` flag analog — model and mode ARE the delegation surface.
67: 
68: ```bash
69: # Default agent mode (read-write, gated by approval flags)
70: cursor-agent -p "Fix the authentication bug in src/auth/handler.ts" \
71:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
72: 
73: # Read-only planning mode
74: cursor-agent -p "Plan the migration from REST to GraphQL" \
75:   --mode plan --model composer-2.5
76: 
77: # Read-only Q&A mode
78: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the retry logic works in src/api/client.ts" \
79:   --mode ask --model composer-2.5
80: ```
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 3. EXECUTION MODE ROSTER
85: 
86: | Mode | Flag | Read/Write | Best For |
87: |------|------|------------|----------|
88: | **Default agent** | (none) | Read-write, gated by `--auto-review`/`--force`/unflagged-prompt | Code generation, fixes, refactoring |
89: | **Plan** | `--mode plan` (shorthand: `--plan`) | Read-only | Multi-step planning without any file writes |
90: | **Ask** | `--mode ask` | Read-only | Q&A, architecture exploration, code explanation |
91: 
92: Approval flags (`--auto-review`/`--force`) have no effect in `--mode plan`/`--mode ask` — both modes are read-only regardless of what approval flag is passed, since there is nothing for the model to write. Headless plan mode does not promise a separate numbered-plan artifact on text stdout; use `--output-format stream-json` for event evidence and inspect content only when an emitted payload exposes it.
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 4. TASK-TYPE ROUTING TABLE
97: 
98: | Task Type | Execution mode | Model guidance |
99: |-----------|-----------------|------------------|
100: | Code review / bug detection | Default agent, `--sandbox enabled`, no write approval needed for the review itself | `composer-2.5` (default) |
101: | Architecture exploration | `--mode ask` | `composer-2.5`, or `cursor-grok-4.6-high`/`-xhigh`/`glm-5.2-max` for deep analysis |
102: | Multi-step planning | `--mode plan` | `composer-2.5` |
103: | Code generation / file edits | Default agent, `--auto-review` (or `--force` for unattended runs) | `composer-2.5` (default) |
104: | Composer-specific validation | Default agent or `--mode ask` | `composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast` explicitly |
105: | Grok/GLM-specific second opinion | Default agent or `--mode ask` | `cursor-grok-4.5-{low,medium,high}[-fast]`, `cursor-grok-4.6-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]`, `grok-4.7-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]`, or `glm-5.2-{high,max}` explicitly |
106: 
107: All model guidance above is scoped to the enforced 29-id allowlist (SKILL.md §3) — never `auto`, never a model outside this table.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ## 5. CURSOR'S NATIVE SUBAGENT SYSTEM (CONTEXT, NOT ORCHESTRATED HERE)
112: 
113: `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` holds Cursor's own skill/subagent system, confirmed live on the reference machine: `automate`, `babysit`, `canvas`, `create-hook`, `create-rule`, `create-skill`, `create-subagent`, `loop`, `migrate-to-skills`, `sdk`, `shell`, `split-to-prs`, `statusline`, `update-cli-config`, `update-cursor-settings`. The presence of `create-subagent` confirms Cursor supports subagents natively, and `create-hook`/`create-rule` confirm native hooks/rules authoring.
114: 
115: This is Cursor-editor-native tooling, not a delegation surface this packet's dispatch adapter controls — a dispatched `cursor-agent -p` session may use its own internal subagents as part of fulfilling the prompt, but this packet does not route to a specific one by name the way `cli-codex` routes to a named `-p <profile>`. Document this distinction accurately rather than inventing a profile-style routing table Cursor does not expose.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## 6. SESSION CONTINUITY
120: 
121: Cursor CLI supports session continuation via `--resume [chatId]` and `--continue`, distinct from a named-profile system:
122: 
123: ```bash
124: # Continue the most recent session
125: cursor-agent -p "Now add tests for what you just implemented" --continue --model composer-2.5
126: 
127: # Resume a specific chat by id (id surfaces in --output-format json's session_id field)
128: cursor-agent -p "Continue implementing the rate limiter" \
129:   --resume "$SESSION_ID" --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
130: ```
131: 
132: ### When to Use Each Operation
133: 
134: | Operation | When to Use |
135: |-----------|--------------|
136: | `--continue` | Immediately following up on the most recent dispatch |
137: | `--resume <chatId>` | Returning to a specific earlier session by its known id |
138: | New session (neither flag) | Fresh context; prior session is not relevant, or re-providing context via the prompt is simpler than tracking a session id |
139: 
140: ### Considerations
141: 
142: - For cross-AI orchestration, it is often simpler to re-provide context in the prompt than to manage `--resume` ids across multiple `cursor-agent -p` calls from a different orchestrating runtime.
143: - Capture `session_id` from `--output-format json` output when a later `--resume` is anticipated.

16: # Cursor CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for all Cursor CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`) is a terminal-based AI coding agent from Cursor, distinct from the Cursor editor but sharing its entire config surface. It dispatches non-interactively via `-p`; this skill defaults dispatch to `composer-2.5` (Cursor's own model) and enforces a 29-id allowlist — Cursor's own `auto` router is deliberately excluded (§5). Unlike sibling CLIs, Cursor has no `--reasoning-effort` flag and no `model[effort=...]` bracket support — effort tiers are baked into the model id itself.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Cursor CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, and troubleshooting guidance.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Setting up or configuring Cursor CLI
35: - Looking up command-line flags or subcommands
36: - Troubleshooting authentication or dispatch issues
37: - Selecting the right model or execution mode for a task
38: - Understanding the shared editor-config surface before a dispatch
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Docs** | https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview |
45: | **Install** | https://cursor.com/install |
46: | **Account** | https://cursor.com |
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. INSTALLATION
51: 
52: | Method | Command | Notes |
53: |--------|---------|-------|
54: | **Install script (macOS/Linux)** | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash` | Downloads the platform-matched binary; installs to `~/.local/bin` |
55: | **Install script (Windows)** | `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' \| iex` | PowerShell installer |
56: | **Verify** | `cursor-agent --version` | Prints the installed build (e.g. `2026.07.23-e383d2b`) |
57: 
58: **Binary naming**: the canonical on-PATH binary is `cursor-agent`; `agent` is an alias symlink to the same binary. Scripts and process-ancestry checks must probe `command -v cursor-agent`, never assume a bare `agent` command.
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS (arm64/x86_64) | Full support |
65: | Linux | Full support |
66: | Windows | Supported via the win32 install script |
67: 
68: After installation, run `cursor-agent` for the interactive mode or `cursor-agent -p "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-cursor authenticates through **Cursor account OAuth** — `cursor-agent login` (browser flow; `NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1` disables automatic browser opening for headless hosts).
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout/status:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Cursor account (opens browser)
80: cursor-agent login
81: 
82: # View authentication status (text output, not a reliable exit code)
83: cursor-agent about
84: 
85: # Log out and clear stored credentials
86: cursor-agent logout
87: ```
88: 
89: **Headless/CI auth:** `CURSOR_API_KEY` env var or `--api-key <key>`. Endpoint override via `--endpoint`/`CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` (default `https://api2.cursor.sh`); custom headers via `-H`/`--header`.
90: 
91: **Auth-state caveat**: `cursor-agent status` can print a misleadingly cached "Login successful" even when the account is not actually authenticated. `cursor-agent about`'s "User Email" field (or a fail-closed `-p` dispatch's output text) is the reliable check — never trust `status` alone, and never trust the dispatch exit code (always `0`, even on auth failure).
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
96: 
97: ### Essential Flags
98: 
99: | Flag | Values | Description |
100: |------|--------|-------------|
101: | `-p` / `--print` | (none) | Non-interactive/print mode — required for orchestrated dispatch |
102: | `--output-format` | `text`, `json`, `stream-json` | `text` (default, final-answer-only), `json` (structured, includes `session_id`), `stream-json` (message-level progress) |
103: | `--stream-partial-output` | (none) | Pairs with `stream-json` for text deltas |
104: | `--model` | one of 29 allowed ids (see §5) | Model to use — `auto` and every other Cursor id are rejected by this skill's dispatch layer |
105: | `--mode` | `plan`, `ask` | `plan` = read-only planning; `ask` = read-only Q&A; omit for the default read-write agent mode (`--plan` is a shorthand for `--mode plan`) |
106: | `--force` / `-f` / `--yolo` | (none) | "Run Everything" — auto-approves unless explicitly denied |
107: | `--auto-review` | (none) | "Smart Auto" — auto-runs safe tool calls, prompts for the rest |
108: | `--sandbox` | `enabled`, `disabled` | Toggles the OS-level sandbox (overrides config) |
109: | `--trust` | (none) | Trusts the workspace without prompting for workspace-trust confirmation |
110: | `--approve-mcps` | (none) | Auto-approves all configured MCP servers |
111: 
112: Headless `--mode plan` guarantees the read-only execution boundary, not a separate numbered-plan artifact on text stdout. Use `--output-format stream-json` when event evidence is required; inspect plan content only when the emitted event payload exposes it.
113: 
114: ### Session & Continuity Flags
115: 
116: | Flag | Description |
117: |------|-------------|
118: | `--resume [chatId]` | Resume a prior chat/session by id |
119: | `--continue` | Continue the most recent session |
120: | `--workspace <path>` | Set the workspace root explicitly |
121: | `--add-dir <path>` | Add an additional accessible directory |
122: | `--plugin-dir <path>` | Add a plugin search directory |
123: 
124: ### Native Worktree Flags (unique surface — see `cursor-tools.md`)
125: 
126: | Flag | Description |
127: |------|-------------|
128: | `-w` / `--worktree [name]` | Start in an isolated git worktree at `~/.cursor/worktrees/<repo>/<name>` |
129: | `--worktree-base <branch>` | Set the base ref for the new worktree |
130: | `--skip-worktree-setup` | Skip setup scripts declared in `.cursor/worktrees.json` |
131: 
132: ### Auth Flags
133: 
134: | Flag | Description |
135: |------|-------------|
136: | `--api-key <key>` | Headless API-key auth |
137: | `-H` / `--header <k:v>` | Custom request header |
138: | `-e` / `--endpoint <url>` | Override the API endpoint |
139: 
140: ### Usage Examples
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Non-interactive default dispatch
144: cursor-agent -p "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await" --model composer-2.5 --output-format text
145: 
146: # With explicit approval + sandbox
147: cursor-agent -p "Add error handling to auth.ts" --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
148: 
149: # Read-only planning
150: cursor-agent -p "Plan a migration to the new API" --mode plan --model composer-2.5
151: 
152: # Read-only Q&A
153: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the retry logic works" --mode ask --model composer-2.5
154: 
155: # Full unattended run
156: cursor-agent -p "Run the test suite and fix failures" --force --sandbox disabled --model composer-2.5
157: 
158: # JSON output (structured, includes session_id)
159: cursor-agent -p "Summarize this module" --output-format json --model composer-2.5
160: ```
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
165: 
166: **Full model catalog (allowlist mirror + enforcement link + effort explanation) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
167: 
168: ### Supported Models — Enforced Allowlist
169: 
170: Cursor's live roster spans 150+ hosted-frontier ids (GPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok/GLM/Kimi families, `cursor-agent --list-models`), with no per-model prompt-craft data for almost all of them and ids that drift over time. **cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids — this is an enforced allowlist, not a reference list.** `auto` (Cursor's own router) is excluded: it can silently resolve to a model outside this set, defeating the point of enforcing one. Enforced at the runtime layer (`CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`; a hard-rejecting check in both `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` before any command is constructed).
171: 
172: Alphabetical by family:
173: 
174: | Family | Allowed ids | Notes |
175: |-------|----|-------|
176: | **Composer** (Cursor-native) ★ default | `composer-2.5`, `composer-2.5-fast` | The direct analog to a provider's own house model — Cursor-exclusive |
177: | **Gemini 3.8** (via Cursor) | `gemini-3.8-flash-high` | Google Gemini 3.8 Flash, High thinking tier only. Cursor displays it as "Gemini 3.8 Flash" — the tier lives in the id suffix; `-low`/`-medium` stay out of scope |
178: | **GLM 5.2** (via Cursor) | `glm-5.2-high`, `glm-5.2-max` | Z.AI's GLM 5.2, 2 tiers |
179: | **GPT-5.6 Luna** (via Cursor) | `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast` | Max thinking tier only, plus its low-latency `-fast` variant. Other Luna tiers and the Sol/Terra personas stay out of scope |
180: | **Grok 4.5** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.5-low`, `cursor-grok-4.5-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.5, 3 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant |
181: | **Grok 4.6** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.6-low`, `cursor-grok-4.6-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.6, all 4 thinking tiers (adds xhigh over 4.5), each with a `-fast` variant |
182: | **Grok 4.7** (via Cursor) | `grok-4.7-low`, `grok-4.7-low-fast`, `grok-4.7-medium`, `grok-4.7-medium-fast`, `grok-4.7-high`, `grok-4.7-high-fast`, `grok-4.7-xhigh`, `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.7, all 4 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant. Cursor lists these ids without the `cursor-` prefix the 4.5 and 4.6 ids carry |
183: 
184: Effort tiers are suffixes on the id (`-low`/`-medium`/`-high`/`-xhigh`/`-fast`/`-max`), not a separate flag. Any id NOT in the table above — including `auto`, every Claude and Kimi id, and every non-curated Gemini or GPT-5.6 tier/persona — is out of scope for this skill; escalate to the user rather than dispatching it. Do not read a family name in the table as blanket permission for that family: only the exact ids listed are enforced.
185: 
186: ### Reasoning Effort Configuration
187: 
188: **There is no `--reasoning-effort` flag, and no `model[effort=...]` parameterized bracket support.** Effort is selected by choosing the exact enumerated id with the desired tier suffix (e.g. `cursor-grok-4.6-high` instead of `cursor-grok-4.6` + a bracket); the bracket form is rejected outright with `Cannot use this model`. Full live-tested detail and the id-form footgun → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
189: 
190: ### Selection Strategy
191: 
192: | Task Type | Model choice | Rationale |
193: |-----------|-----------------|-----------|
194: | General delegation | `composer-2.5` (default) | Cursor's own model; predictable and always allowed |
195: | Task specifically wants Cursor's own model | `composer-2.5` / `composer-2.5-fast` | Cursor-exclusive, no hosted-provider equivalent |
196: | Task specifically wants Gemini, GLM, GPT-5.6 Luna, or Grok at a tier | An exact allowed id (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `glm-5.2-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) | Effort is baked into the id; only these 27 non-Composer ids are permitted |
197: | Task wants any model outside the allowlist | **Not supported** | Escalate to the user — do not substitute an allowed model silently |
198: 
199: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it defaults to `composer-2.5`, never `auto`.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
204: 
205: ### Print Mode Output
206: 
207: `cursor-agent -p` writes its final answer to stdout in `text` mode (default). Use `--output-format json` for structured output including `session_id`, `usage`, and `request_id`.
208: 
209: ```bash
210: # Capture to file
211: cursor-agent -p "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" \
212:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format text > /tmp/user-interface.ts
213: 
214: # Capture structured JSON (includes session_id)
215: cursor-agent -p "List all exported functions in src/" \
216:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format json > /tmp/result.json
217: jq -r '.result' /tmp/result.json
218: 
219: # Redirect stderr separately
220: cursor-agent -p "Analyze auth flow" --model composer-2.5 > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
221: ```
222: 
223: ### Exit Codes
224: 
225: | Code | Meaning |
226: |------|---------|
227: | `0` | Process completed — **NOT proof of success or authentication**; always inspect output text |
228: | Non-zero | A CLI-level failure (e.g. invalid flag) — this is the ONE case exit code is meaningful |
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 7. WORKSPACE TRUST
233: 
234: Cursor Agent can execute code and access files in the target directory. On an untrusted directory, a dispatch fails with a "Workspace Trust Required" error unless `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` is passed. For orchestrated repo-scoped dispatches inside a repo the operator already trusts, pass `--trust` (or rely on `--force` already implying trust).
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ## 8. RULES SOURCES
239: 
240: Cursor CLI reads project rules from multiple sources, applied automatically: `.cursor/rules` (directory), `AGENTS.md` (project root), `CLAUDE.md` (project root), and legacy `.cursorrules`. A dispatched session in this repo picks up `AGENTS.md` at the repo root automatically — relevant when composing a delegation prompt, since the delegated session already has this project's governing rules loaded.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## 9. MCP INTEGRATION
245: 
246: `cursor-agent mcp` subcommands: `login <id>`, `list`, `list-tools <id>`, `enable <id>`, `disable <id>`. Config file: `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (user) — "the CLI uses the same configuration as the editor". Precedence: project → global → nested. `enable <id>` is an operator trust mutation; a configured but unapproved server is a manual-playbook SKIP with blocker `MCP server is configured but not approved; operator must run cursor-agent mcp enable <id> outside playbook`. `--approve-mcps` auto-approves all configured servers for a dispatch, not for this trust-state inspection. Cursor CLI is an MCP *client* only — it discovers and uses configured servers; there is no documented mode of it acting as an MCP server itself.
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ## 10. SUBCOMMANDS
251: 
252: | Subcommand | Description |
253: |------------|-------------|
254: | `cursor-agent -p "<prompt>"` | Non-interactive execution — runs a single prompt and exits |
255: | `cursor-agent login` / `logout` | Authenticate / clear credentials via Cursor account OAuth |
256: | `cursor-agent status` / `whoami` | Session/account status (caution: `status` can show stale cached state) |
257: | `cursor-agent about` | Reliable account/auth info, including CLI version and login email |
258: | `cursor-agent models` | List available models (requires authentication) |
259: | `cursor-agent mcp <subcommand>` | Manage MCP server connections |
260: | `cursor-agent plugin marketplace` | Manage plugins and plugin marketplaces |
261: | `cursor-agent worker` | Run a private cloud worker (see `cursor-tools.md`) |
262: | `cursor-agent install-shell-integration` / `uninstall-shell-integration` | Manage shell integration |
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: ## 11. TROUBLESHOOTING
267: 
268: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
269: |---------|-------|----------|
270: | Output contains `Error: Authentication required` (exit `0`) | Not authenticated | Run `cursor-agent login`, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY` |
271: | `cursor-agent status` says "Login successful" but `about` says "Not logged in" | `status` uses a stale cache | Trust `about`'s "User Email" field, not `status` |
272: | `Workspace Trust Required` | Directory not yet trusted | Pass `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` |
273: | `Cannot use this model: <id>[...]` | Parameterized model bracket, not supported | Use an exact enumerated id from `--list-models` |
274: | Task ran but no files changed | `--mode plan`/`--mode ask` used, or neither `--auto-review` nor `--force` was passed | Use the default agent mode with an approval flag for edit tasks |
275: | `command not found: cursor-agent` | Not installed or PATH not updated | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash`; verify with `which cursor-agent` |
276: | Unexpected hook fires, or dispatch behaves per operator's editor config | Shared `.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/` config surface | See `shared-editor-config.md` for the isolation implications |
277: | Under `--sandbox enabled`, a dispatched command that calls the skill-advisor CLI gets `degraded: true`, `source: "local-scorer"` and no `freshness` | The CLI answers from its local scorer only when it cannot reach the advisor daemon. The live daemon listens on a Unix socket under `/tmp/system-skill-advisor/`, outside the workspace (resolved by `.skilled/bin/lib/launcher-ipc-bridge.cjs`), and the sandboxed command did not reach it. Three Grok 4.7 dispatches showed this, and the same calls with the sandbox disabled got the live answer | Dispatch with `--sandbox disabled` when the task needs the live advisor answer. Otherwise treat the degraded answer as the sandbox's limit, not an advisor fault |
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 12. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
282: 
283: | Variable | Purpose |
284: |----------|---------|
285: | `CURSOR_API_KEY` | Headless API-key authentication |
286: | `CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` | Override the default API endpoint (`https://api2.cursor.sh`) |
287: | `CURSOR_AGENT` | Confirmed live: set to `1` unconditionally whenever the current process runs under `cursor-agent` — the primary self-invocation-guard signal |
288: | `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` | Confirmed live: the active session/chat id, matching `--output-format json`'s `session_id` field |
289: | `CURSOR_INVOKED_AS` | Confirmed live: how the binary was invoked (`cursor-agent`) |
290: | `NO_OPEN_BROWSER` | Disables automatic browser opening during `cursor-agent login` |

129: | `--worktree-base <branch>` | Set the base ref for the new worktree |
130: | `--skip-worktree-setup` | Skip setup scripts declared in `.cursor/worktrees.json` |
131: 
132: ### Auth Flags
133: 
134: | Flag | Description |
135: |------|-------------|
136: | `--api-key <key>` | Headless API-key auth |
137: | `-H` / `--header <k:v>` | Custom request header |
138: | `-e` / `--endpoint <url>` | Override the API endpoint |
139: 
140: ### Usage Examples
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Non-interactive default dispatch
144: cursor-agent -p "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await" --model composer-2.5 --output-format text
145: 
146: # With explicit approval + sandbox
147: cursor-agent -p "Add error handling to auth.ts" --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
148: 
149: # Read-only planning
150: cursor-agent -p "Plan a migration to the new API" --mode plan --model composer-2.5
151: 
152: # Read-only Q&A
153: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the retry logic works" --mode ask --model composer-2.5
154: 
155: # Full unattended run
156: cursor-agent -p "Run the test suite and fix failures" --force --sandbox disabled --model composer-2.5
157: 
158: # JSON output (structured, includes session_id)
159: cursor-agent -p "Summarize this module" --output-format json --model composer-2.5
160: ```
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
165: 
166: **Full model catalog (allowlist mirror + enforcement link + effort explanation) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
167: 
168: ### Supported Models — Enforced Allowlist
169: 
170: Cursor's live roster spans 150+ hosted-frontier ids (GPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok/GLM/Kimi families, `cursor-agent --list-models`), with no per-model prompt-craft data for almost all of them and ids that drift over time. **cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids — this is an enforced allowlist, not a reference list.** `auto` (Cursor's own router) is excluded: it can silently resolve to a model outside this set, defeating the point of enforcing one. Enforced at the runtime layer (`CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`; a hard-rejecting check in both `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` before any command is constructed).
171: 
172: Alphabetical by family:
173: 
174: | Family | Allowed ids | Notes |
175: |-------|----|-------|
176: | **Composer** (Cursor-native) ★ default | `composer-2.5`, `composer-2.5-fast` | The direct analog to a provider's own house model — Cursor-exclusive |
177: | **Gemini 3.8** (via Cursor) | `gemini-3.8-flash-high` | Google Gemini 3.8 Flash, High thinking tier only. Cursor displays it as "Gemini 3.8 Flash" — the tier lives in the id suffix; `-low`/`-medium` stay out of scope |
178: | **GLM 5.2** (via Cursor) | `glm-5.2-high`, `glm-5.2-max` | Z.AI's GLM 5.2, 2 tiers |
179: | **GPT-5.6 Luna** (via Cursor) | `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast` | Max thinking tier only, plus its low-latency `-fast` variant. Other Luna tiers and the Sol/Terra personas stay out of scope |
180: | **Grok 4.5** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.5-low`, `cursor-grok-4.5-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.5, 3 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant |
181: | **Grok 4.6** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.6-low`, `cursor-grok-4.6-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.6, all 4 thinking tiers (adds xhigh over 4.5), each with a `-fast` variant |
182: | **Grok 4.7** (via Cursor) | `grok-4.7-low`, `grok-4.7-low-fast`, `grok-4.7-medium`, `grok-4.7-medium-fast`, `grok-4.7-high`, `grok-4.7-high-fast`, `grok-4.7-xhigh`, `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.7, all 4 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant. Cursor lists these ids without the `cursor-` prefix the 4.5 and 4.6 ids carry |
183: 
184: Effort tiers are suffixes on the id (`-low`/`-medium`/`-high`/`-xhigh`/`-fast`/`-max`), not a separate flag. Any id NOT in the table above — including `auto`, every Claude and Kimi id, and every non-curated Gemini or GPT-5.6 tier/persona — is out of scope for this skill; escalate to the user rather than dispatching it. Do not read a family name in the table as blanket permission for that family: only the exact ids listed are enforced.
185: 
186: ### Reasoning Effort Configuration
187: 
188: **There is no `--reasoning-effort` flag, and no `model[effort=...]` parameterized bracket support.** Effort is selected by choosing the exact enumerated id with the desired tier suffix (e.g. `cursor-grok-4.6-high` instead of `cursor-grok-4.6` + a bracket); the bracket form is rejected outright with `Cannot use this model`. Full live-tested detail and the id-form footgun → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
189: 
190: ### Selection Strategy
191: 
192: | Task Type | Model choice | Rationale |
193: |-----------|-----------------|-----------|
194: | General delegation | `composer-2.5` (default) | Cursor's own model; predictable and always allowed |
195: | Task specifically wants Cursor's own model | `composer-2.5` / `composer-2.5-fast` | Cursor-exclusive, no hosted-provider equivalent |
196: | Task specifically wants Gemini, GLM, GPT-5.6 Luna, or Grok at a tier | An exact allowed id (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `glm-5.2-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) | Effort is baked into the id; only these 27 non-Composer ids are permitted |
197: | Task wants any model outside the allowlist | **Not supported** | Escalate to the user — do not substitute an allowed model silently |
198: 
199: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it defaults to `composer-2.5`, never `auto`.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
204: 
205: ### Print Mode Output
206: 
207: `cursor-agent -p` writes its final answer to stdout in `text` mode (default). Use `--output-format json` for structured output including `session_id`, `usage`, and `request_id`.
208: 
209: ```bash
210: # Capture to file
211: cursor-agent -p "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" \
212:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format text > /tmp/user-interface.ts
213: 
214: # Capture structured JSON (includes session_id)
215: cursor-agent -p "List all exported functions in src/" \
216:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format json > /tmp/result.json
217: jq -r '.result' /tmp/result.json
218: 
219: # Redirect stderr separately
220: cursor-agent -p "Analyze auth flow" --model composer-2.5 > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
221: ```
222: 
223: ### Exit Codes
224: 
225: | Code | Meaning |
226: |------|---------|
227: | `0` | Process completed — **NOT proof of success or authentication**; always inspect output text |
228: | Non-zero | A CLI-level failure (e.g. invalid flag) — this is the ONE case exit code is meaningful |
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 7. WORKSPACE TRUST
233: 
234: Cursor Agent can execute code and access files in the target directory. On an untrusted directory, a dispatch fails with a "Workspace Trust Required" error unless `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` is passed. For orchestrated repo-scoped dispatches inside a repo the operator already trusts, pass `--trust` (or rely on `--force` already implying trust).
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ## 8. RULES SOURCES
239: 
240: Cursor CLI reads project rules from multiple sources, applied automatically: `.cursor/rules` (directory), `AGENTS.md` (project root), `CLAUDE.md` (project root), and legacy `.cursorrules`. A dispatched session in this repo picks up `AGENTS.md` at the repo root automatically — relevant when composing a delegation prompt, since the delegated session already has this project's governing rules loaded.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## 9. MCP INTEGRATION
245: 
246: `cursor-agent mcp` subcommands: `login <id>`, `list`, `list-tools <id>`, `enable <id>`, `disable <id>`. Config file: `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (user) — "the CLI uses the same configuration as the editor". Precedence: project → global → nested. `enable <id>` is an operator trust mutation; a configured but unapproved server is a manual-playbook SKIP with blocker `MCP server is configured but not approved; operator must run cursor-agent mcp enable <id> outside playbook`. `--approve-mcps` auto-approves all configured servers for a dispatch, not for this trust-state inspection. Cursor CLI is an MCP *client* only — it discovers and uses configured servers; there is no documented mode of it acting as an MCP server itself.
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ## 10. SUBCOMMANDS
251: 
252: | Subcommand | Description |
253: |------------|-------------|
254: | `cursor-agent -p "<prompt>"` | Non-interactive execution — runs a single prompt and exits |
255: | `cursor-agent login` / `logout` | Authenticate / clear credentials via Cursor account OAuth |
256: | `cursor-agent status` / `whoami` | Session/account status (caution: `status` can show stale cached state) |
257: | `cursor-agent about` | Reliable account/auth info, including CLI version and login email |
258: | `cursor-agent models` | List available models (requires authentication) |
259: | `cursor-agent mcp <subcommand>` | Manage MCP server connections |
260: | `cursor-agent plugin marketplace` | Manage plugins and plugin marketplaces |
261: | `cursor-agent worker` | Run a private cloud worker (see `cursor-tools.md`) |
262: | `cursor-agent install-shell-integration` / `uninstall-shell-integration` | Manage shell integration |
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: ## 11. TROUBLESHOOTING
267: 
268: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
269: |---------|-------|----------|
270: | Output contains `Error: Authentication required` (exit `0`) | Not authenticated | Run `cursor-agent login`, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY` |
271: | `cursor-agent status` says "Login successful" but `about` says "Not logged in" | `status` uses a stale cache | Trust `about`'s "User Email" field, not `status` |
272: | `Workspace Trust Required` | Directory not yet trusted | Pass `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` |
273: | `Cannot use this model: <id>[...]` | Parameterized model bracket, not supported | Use an exact enumerated id from `--list-models` |
274: | Task ran but no files changed | `--mode plan`/`--mode ask` used, or neither `--auto-review` nor `--force` was passed | Use the default agent mode with an approval flag for edit tasks |
275: | `command not found: cursor-agent` | Not installed or PATH not updated | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash`; verify with `which cursor-agent` |
276: | Unexpected hook fires, or dispatch behaves per operator's editor config | Shared `.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/` config surface | See `shared-editor-config.md` for the isolation implications |
277: | Under `--sandbox enabled`, a dispatched command that calls the skill-advisor CLI gets `degraded: true`, `source: "local-scorer"` and no `freshness` | The CLI answers from its local scorer only when it cannot reach the advisor daemon. The live daemon listens on a Unix socket under `/tmp/system-skill-advisor/`, outside the workspace (resolved by `.skilled/bin/lib/launcher-ipc-bridge.cjs`), and the sandboxed command did not reach it. Three Grok 4.7 dispatches showed this, and the same calls with the sandbox disabled got the live answer | Dispatch with `--sandbox disabled` when the task needs the live advisor answer. Otherwise treat the degraded answer as the sandbox's limit, not an advisor fault |
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 12. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
282: 
283: | Variable | Purpose |
284: |----------|---------|
285: | `CURSOR_API_KEY` | Headless API-key authentication |
286: | `CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` | Override the default API endpoint (`https://api2.cursor.sh`) |
287: | `CURSOR_AGENT` | Confirmed live: set to `1` unconditionally whenever the current process runs under `cursor-agent` — the primary self-invocation-guard signal |
288: | `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` | Confirmed live: the active session/chat id, matching `--output-format json`'s `session_id` field |
289: | `CURSOR_INVOKED_AS` | Confirmed live: how the binary was invoked (`cursor-agent`) |
290: | `NO_OPEN_BROWSER` | Disables automatic browser opening during `cursor-agent login` |

14: 
15: # Cursor CLI Unique Capabilities
16: 
17: Reference for the Cursor CLI surfaces that have **no analog** in `cli-codex`, `cli-claude-code`, or `cli-opencode`. Each is documented as an opt-in escape hatch — this packet's default dispatch (`SKILL.md` §3) never invokes any of them automatically.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Core Principle
24: 
25: Cursor CLI ships several capabilities that go beyond "run a prompt against a model": native git worktree isolation, a private cloud execution worker, a plugin marketplace, and Cursor's own subagent/skill system. None of these change `cli-cursor`'s `packetKind: "workflow"` classification (see `030-cli-cursor-creation/003-cli-cursor-skill-packet/decision-record.md` ADR-001) — the packet's default dispatch still runs locally and writes land in this repo's checkout. These surfaces are documented here as deliberate, user-invoked escape hatches.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - The operator explicitly wants an experiment tried in an isolated checkout without touching the current workspace
30: - The operator explicitly wants Cursor to run agents in a remote/cloud environment rather than locally
31: - The operator wants to discover or manage Cursor plugins
32: - A task needs an MCP server Cursor is already configured to use
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 2. NATIVE GIT WORKTREE ISOLATION
37: 
38: ### What It Is
39: 
40: `-w` / `--worktree [name]` starts `cursor-agent` in an isolated git worktree at `~/.cursor/worktrees/<reponame>/<name>`, rather than the current working directory. `--worktree-base <branch>` sets the base ref for the new worktree. `--skip-worktree-setup` skips any setup scripts declared in `.cursor/worktrees.json`.
41: 
42: ### Why It's Out of Scope for Orchestrated Dispatch
43: 
44: This repo already manages its own numbered-worktree discipline via `sk-git` (owner-scoped branches, `.worktrees/{NNNN}-{owner}-{slug}` directories). A dispatched `cursor-agent` inside a deep-loop fan-out lineage already runs inside that lineage's own isolated directory — passing `-w` on top would create a SECOND, Cursor-native worktree nested inside or alongside the first, doubling isolation in a way the runtime does not expect and has not been built to reconcile. The deep-loop executor adapter (`buildCursorLineageCommand`, added in the executor-support phase of this creation packet) never passes `-w`.
45: 
46: ### When an Operator Might Use It Directly
47: 
48: ```bash
49: # Try a risky refactor in a disposable worktree, leaving the current checkout untouched
50: cursor-agent -p "Attempt an aggressive refactor of the auth module" \
51:   -w risky-refactor --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
52: 
53: # Base the new worktree on a specific branch
54: cursor-agent -p "Prototype the new caching layer" \
55:   -w cache-prototype --worktree-base develop --model composer-2.5
56: ```
57: 
58: This is a direct, interactive/manual operator action — not something an orchestrated fan-out or automated pipeline in this repo should invoke on its own.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 3. CLOUD WORKER
63: 
64: ### What It Is
65: 
66: `cursor-agent worker` runs a private cloud worker that connects to Cursor's infrastructure to run agents in the operator's own environment remotely. It is infra-grade remote execution: Kubernetes-style health probes (`GET /healthz`, `/readyz`), a Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, pool vs. shared assignment (`--pool`/`--pool-name`), labels, and `--auth-token-file` for operator-managed secret mounts.
67: 
68: ### Why It's Out of Scope for This Packet's Runtime Wiring
69: 
70: This is a fundamentally different execution shape than every other capability this packet dispatches — it stands up a long-running service, not a single bounded `-p` prompt/response round-trip. Wiring it into this repo's deep-loop runtime would mean building an entirely separate execution model (service lifecycle, health checks, secret mounts) that no sibling CLI needs and that the parent packet's spec explicitly scopes out. If a future need for genuinely remote, infra-grade Cursor execution arises, that is new scope for a dedicated future packet — not a repurposing of this one's `-p` dispatch adapter.
71: 
72: ### When an Operator Might Use It Directly
73: 
74: ```bash
75: # Start a worker (operator-run, not orchestrated by this packet)
76: cursor-agent worker --pool my-pool --auth-token-file ~/.cursor/worker-token
77: ```
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 4. PLUGIN MARKETPLACE
82: 
83: ### What It Is
84: 
85: `cursor-agent plugin marketplace` manages plugins and plugin marketplaces, stored under `~/.cursor/plugins/`. This is analogous to an editor extension system, not a per-dispatch flag — it changes what capabilities are available to `cursor-agent` sessions going forward, not the current dispatch alone.
86: 
87: ### Relevance to Orchestrated Dispatch
88: 
89: Plugins are a shared, persistent, operator-controlled surface (like the shared editor config — see `shared-editor-config.md`). This packet's dispatch adapter does not install, enable, or disable plugins as part of a delegation; a dispatched session simply inherits whatever plugins are already installed. If a task specifically needs marketplace management, that is an explicit operator action, not something to embed in an automated dispatch prompt.
90: 
91: ```bash
92: # Operator-run: discover and manage plugins directly
93: cursor-agent plugin marketplace
94: ```
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 5. MCP CLIENT SUPPORT
99: 
100: ### What It Is
101: 
102: `cursor-agent mcp` subcommands manage MCP server connections: `login <id>`, `list`, `list-tools <id>`, `enable <id>`, `disable <id>`. Configuration lives in `.cursor/mcp.json` (project scope) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (user scope) — the same files the Cursor editor reads (see `shared-editor-config.md`). `enable <id>` is an operator-controlled trust mutation and must not be run by the manual playbook. If a configured server is not approved, record `SKIP: MCP server is configured but not approved; operator must run cursor-agent mcp enable <id> outside playbook`.
103: 
104: ### Relevance to Orchestrated Dispatch
105: 
106: Cursor CLI is an MCP **client** only — it discovers and uses already-configured MCP servers. There is no documented mode of `cursor-agent` acting as an MCP server itself. When a dispatched task genuinely needs MCP tool access and the operator's `.cursor/mcp.json` already has the right servers configured, pass `--approve-mcps` to avoid blocking on an interactive approval the unattended dispatch can never answer:
107: 
108: ```bash
109: cursor-agent -p "Use the configured GitHub MCP server to list open PRs" \
110:   --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled --approve-mcps
111: ```
112: 
113: Without `--approve-mcps`, an unapproved MCP server prompt behaves like any other unattended approval — nothing can answer it, and the action stalls or is silently skipped depending on the approval mode in effect. `--approve-mcps` applies to a single dispatch; it is not a replacement for the explicit operator approval required by the `mcp list`/`list-tools` playbook scenario.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## 6. SUMMARY TABLE
118: 
119: | Surface | Flag/subcommand | Default in this packet's dispatch | Orchestrated fan-out use |
120: |---|---|---|---|
121: | Native worktree | `-w`/`--worktree` | Never passed | Not wired — would double-isolate against the runtime's own lineage directories |
122: | Cloud worker | `cursor-agent worker` | Never invoked | Out of scope — different execution shape entirely |
123: | Plugin marketplace | `cursor-agent plugin marketplace` | Never invoked | Operator-only, persistent/shared surface |
124: | MCP client | `cursor-agent mcp ...` / `--approve-mcps` | `--approve-mcps` passed when a task explicitly needs MCP tools | Supported, gated by explicit task need |
